SMTO-LLM-0005 — Model server connection closed

GUID: ab0d96be-86cd-48dc-aec3-a070864000b8
Slug: llm-connection-closed
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model's answer stopped partway through because the connection ended. SMTO won't guess the missing part, so only this one model reply is lost.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card and select Check saved model. This shows whether the model server is back to answering completely.
  2. If it fails, or answers keep getting cut off, ask the person who runs the model server to check its log and any proxy in front of it. A server restart or a proxy with a time or size limit can end the connection early.
  3. When the check passes, start a new task. Don't redo steps the earlier task already finished. Earlier finished steps already took effect; only the last model reply was incomplete.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model passes and the next task gets complete answers.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model server. Don't turn off security checks to work around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model connection ended (EOF, incomplete read, broken pipe or remote disconnect) before a complete response was received.

What this means

  • End-of-file, an incomplete read or an abrupt peer disconnect left the response unfinished. This does not establish a provider crash or a failed tool operation. Only the affected model decision is incomplete; prior work remains governed by its receipts.

Why this can happen

  • The peer or an intermediary ended the response early; an incomplete read can also indicate a truncated transfer.

How to diagnose it

  • Check whether the provider recorded a completed response and whether a proxy closed the stream earlier. Compare the last stream event with the expected completion marker.

How to fix it

  • Ask the provider operator to check provider and proxy logs for the interrupted stream (crash, restart, idle timeout or response size limit on a reverse proxy), then verify with Check saved model. Prior completed tool work is unaffected and should not be replayed.
  • Ask the provider operator to inspect the interrupted stream and any proxy limits before testing another model request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The next diagnostic response arrives completely and has a valid completion marker.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Typed transport exception (or exact legacy standard reason where supported); no tool outcome is inferred from connection state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
